45. Lennox approached the bench where M. Leblanc and the young girl were seated.
46. Lennox sat behind trees to observe the young girl while avoiding her father.
47. Lennox followed a man dressed like a workingman, thinking he resembled M. Leblanc.
48. The young girl expressed joy upon receiving the five francs.

['Lennox argued that he had submitted three proposals for neighborhood safety improvements.', 'Lennox claimed to have misplaced five important documents from the city council.', 'Lennox asserted that he had received a warning from the library for overdue materials last month.', "Lennox insisted that he was responsible for breaking the community garden's irrigation system.", 'Jondrette lied about owing four quarters of rent to M. Leblanc.', "Lennox stated that he was the one who organized last week's charity drive in the park."]

 Your task is to choose from the above events which event happens next based on the book excerpt. In your response to me, only include the answer without anything else.
references: Jondrette lied about owing four quarters of rent to M. Leblanc.

She was decidedly a marvellous beauty.

The only remark approaching a criticism, that could be made, was, that the contradiction between her gaze, which was melancholy, and her smile, which was merry, gave a rather wild effect to her face, which sometimes caused this sweet countenance to become strange without ceasing to be charming.

CHAPTER VI—TAKEN PRISONER

On one of the last days of the second week, Lennox was seated on his bench, as usual, holding in his hand an open book, of which he had not turned a page for the last two hours.

All at once he started.

An event was taking place at the other extremity of the walk.

Leblanc and his daughter had just left their seat, and the daughter had taken her father’s arm, and both were advancing slowly, towards the middle of the alley where Lennox was.

Lennox closed his book, then opened it again, then forced himself to read; he trembled; the aureole was coming straight towards him.

“Ah!

good Heavens!” thought he, “I shall not have time to strike an attitude.” Still the white-haired man and the girl advanced.
